subject: dplyr collect() continues to hit database after bringing data into data.frame

messages.author: a41fdfda1674e056
messages.subject: dplyr collect() continues to hit database after bringing data into data.frame
parts:
I've encountered a situation with dplyr where it appears using collect() doesn't sever the umbilical cord to the database you originally query from.

I was previously loading data from a csv file with fread and converting it to a tbl_df, then applying group_by and applying do().

E.g.,

## Get Data
data <- tbl_dt(fread(file))
## group and operate on data
data <- data %.%
    filter((region %in% regions)) %.% 
    mutate(time = as.POSIXct(time), type = make.names(paste(region, type))) %.%
    group_by(date, type) %.% do(head(., 1)) %.% 
    ungroup() %.% select(date, type, time)

Then I tried to convert my process to querying data from a centralized postgres database and uploaded by data there.

I created my database connection here:

## Get Data
    tmp <- src_postgres(dbname = "postgres", user = "postgres", password = "xxxxx")
    data_postgres <- tbl(tmp, "data")
    c1 <- select(data_postgres, time, date, region, type)
    data <- collect(c1)
## group and operate on data
data <- data %.%
    filter((region %in% regions)) %.% 
    mutate(time = as.POSIXct(time), type = make.names(paste(region, type))) %.%
    group_by(date, type) %.% do(head(., 1)) %.% 
    ungroup() %.% select(date, type, time)

This appeared to bring in the table from the database and put it in a local data.frame in R memory.

However, when I subsequently went on to the grouping operations it would show a progress bar and what previously was instantaneous in memory, would take a minute, and would show an output of time spent like ===Completed after 1 m   . The above operation applying group_by and do to the df read from disk was instantaneous.

Is there anyway to bring data in from the database into a data.frame and continue operating as if you had read it directly from disk?

I also found that do() on collected data from a database wouldn't be able to refer to the column names in the scope anymore, whereas a dataframe created by reading from disk you could.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: dplyr collect() continues to hit database after bringing data into data.frame
parts:
Take a look at str(data), that will tell you whether it's still
connected to the database or not. The code for collect is very
simple, so I'd be surprised if it wasn't working correctly.

Hadley
